transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, thank you. Well, I'm here because... I guess, honestly, I've just been having a really hard time lately. I'm a computer systems analyst, and I actually just finished my graduate program a bit ago, so I was doing really, really well. Like, I was on top of everything, managing all these complex projects, and I was good at it. They even promoted me recently. But... I don't know, lately I just can't shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. It's just this constant thought looping in my head. 

And it's not just the environment, it's me. I feel like I'm somehow completely damaged now. I sit at my desk and I just look at the screen and think about how the competent, capable person who actually earned that promotion... it's like she isn't really there anymore. I feel like she's gone and I've been replaced by this broken version of myself, and no matter how much I try to logic my way out of it—because I work with systems and logic all day, you know?—I just keep coming back to this deep-seated belief that I'm ruined and nothing is secure anymore. It's just exhausting, constantly feeling like everything is fundamentally wrong with me now.
Do you experience thoughts that keep coming into your mind, even when you don't want them, that feel intrusive or disturbing to you?

Yeah. Yes, I do. It's... it's like my brain just hijacks me, honestly. I'll just be trying to work, or even just trying to relax, which is a joke lately, but I'll be trying, and then something so small will happen. Like... okay, so at work, we have these badge scanners, right? They make this very specific, sharp little beep when you swipe in. And if I hear that beep, or even just someone walking with heavy footsteps down the hallway near my cubicle, or... or even if my phone buzzes with a late-night deployment alert—which happens all the time in my job, we do server updates at like 2 AM—if any of those things happen, it's just... BAM. 

I'm not at my desk anymore. I'm not in my apartment. I am instantly, completely ripped right back to that office. My chest gets so incredibly tight, like someone is sitting on my ribs, and I can't pull in a full breath. And then the image just flashes into my head, so clearly it's like a movie playing behind my eyes, and I see the security guard just... lying on the floor. And it cuts through absolutely everything. I could be in the middle of writing a really complex piece of code, or trying to explain a system architecture to a client, and suddenly I can't see the screen, I can't hear the person talking to me, I just see him on the floor. And I don't want to think about it! I really, really don't. I try so hard to push it away and focus on the data, focus on the logic, but it just forces its way in and completely derails me. It's like I have zero control over my own mind anymore, which is terrifying because my mind is my whole career. It just happens over and over and over.

The adjustment disorder specifier 'with mixed anxiety and depressed mood' accounts for both the anxious intrusions and the depressive symptoms described.
